A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Implicit In-context Learning (I2CL). Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across three model architectures, together with ablations, demonstration-robustness tests, and transfer-learning results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated baselines, Llama3-8B results, synthetic-data experiments, and a combined ICL+I2CL evaluation.

M1.justification: The core context vectorization, injection, noisy calibration, and transfer algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds an ICL+I2CL variant that retains demonstration tokens during both calibration and inference, providing a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: The nine natural-language classification datasets are retained. v2 Appendix C.2 adds a synthetic three-class task distinguishing random strings, special characters, and numerical values, labeled A, B, and C.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add six evaluated comparators: ICV, AutoCompressors, ICAE, CEPE, LoRA, and IA3. This substantially broadens comparison to activation steering, trained context compression, and parameter-efficient adaptation. v1's Soft-prompt is retained as Prompt-tuning in Table 2; the GPT-J and GPT2-XL comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama3-8B evaluation, extends the I2CL shot-count sweep from 1–10 to 1–1,000 examples per class, and introduces PEFT and pretrained-compressor evaluation protocols. The combined-method experiment covers eight tasks, excluding AGNews for memory reasons. Evaluation sampling is described as validation/test data rather than uniformly sampled development data; this wording change does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends shot-count sensitivity analysis and adds synthetic-data tests of dependence on semantic/formatting priors, combination with ICL, and class-wise context-vector visualizations. Conversely, v1's vectorization ablation comparing concatenation, PCA, and averaging is removed, including Table 7 and its discussion. Most other ablations and demonstration-robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and retain uncertainty values alongside scores. However, v2 removes v1 Table 1's explicit statement identifying these as means and standard deviations, without replacing that explanation elsewhere. No increase in runs or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Original headline I2CL scores remain unchanged, including 75.12% on Llama2-7b. Substantial new results cover the added baselines, Llama3, extended scaling, and supplementary analyses. Table 14 reports synthetic-task accuracy of 86.48% for I2CL versus 66.20% for ICL; Table 15 reports 81.96% for the combination versus 75.21% for ICL over eight tasks. Prompt-tuning's HateSpeech18 score changes from 59.56% to 49.56%, while its reported average remains 54.94%. The removed vectorization ablation also removes result entries.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematical definitions, Equations 1–7, and transfer-learning algorithm are retained. Neither version supplies formal proofs. The removed two-stage interpretation of ICL is an informal hypothesis rather than a mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about few-shot-level performance at zero-shot inference cost, demonstration robustness, and task identifiers remain. v2 narrows the conclusion to potential utility in constrained scenarios and refocuses the third contribution from understanding ICL's mechanisms toward examining I2CL's own design and mechanisms.

C2.justification: v2 removes the hypothetical two-stage explanation of conventional ICL from v1 Section 5. It adds interpretations of calibration's role, within-task label information and the EmoC exception, and combining I2CL with ICL when inference resources permit. It explicitly declines overall superiority over long-context compressors and adds the concern that implicit vectors complicate detection of malicious content. The principal classification-only and model-access limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 substantially expands reproduction information: ICV example pairing, strength searches and per-task values; released-model sources and defaults for three compressors; and PEFT implementation settings. LoRA details include rank 8, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, and learning rate 0.001. v2 also clarifies that the deficient-demonstration selection hold-out does not overlap training or evaluation data. The I2CL code link and principal calibration settings remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive prompt-compression positioning section, citing Chang, Chevalier, Ge, and Yen and distinguishing amortized compression from direct residual-stream intervention. PEFT comparisons introduce Hu et al. and Liu et al. (2022), while activation-engineering coverage adds Li et al. (2025). Earlier positioning around corroborating linear representations and its Mikolov, Meng, and Hernandez (2023) references is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental narrative receive extensive editing. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 4, benchmarking is reorganized by comparator category, and Discussion is replaced by a dedicated Limitations section. Potential-design discussion moves into Appendix D, and the appendices gain a contents list and reorganized subsections.

P2.justification: Table 1 is transposed and regrouped, with a separate PEFT table and several new appendix tables. The method schematic is reduced and relocated; the scaling plot is expanded and moved into the main text. Nine existing coefficient plots are consolidated into Figure 6, and class-wise visualizations are added as Figure 7. The vectorization-ablation table is removed, alongside broader conference-format layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added PEFT and compression comparisons better test I2CL against plausible practical alternatives, while expanded scaling and synthetic analyses strengthen its empirical assessment. These benefits are tempered by removal of the vectorization ablation and new reporting inconsistencies. In particular, Table 13 reports Llama3 averages of 81.26% and 81.18%, although its listed task scores average approximately 72.23% and 72.17%; Table 2 also retains an inconsistent prompt-tuning average. The revision offers a useful but limited net quality improvement.
